spec: AES MixColumns (forward), a 32x32 GF(2) linear map. Column matrix [[2,3,1,1],[1,2,3,1],[1,1,2,3],[3,1,1,2]] over GF(2^8) with reduction polynomial 0x11b.
note: sha256_circuit_json is over the exact circuit JSON file bytes as written. sha256_canonical_gates is SHA-256 over the exact UTF-8 bytes of the compact JSON string {"inputCount":32,"gates":[...]} with keys in that order; reproduce it with scripts/reproduce_canonical_hashes.py.

circuits.outputConvention: output j (j in 0..31) is MixColumns output bit j; bit j = bit (j mod 8) of state byte (j div 8), least-significant-bit-first within each byte. It is produced at internal signal index outputSignals[j].

verified.method: checked against AES MixColumns rebuilt from GF(2^8) in verify.py, and against 32 basis-vector responses in the Verilog testbench

circuits.provenance: Found by this project's own search from scratch, with no imported material anywhere in the chain: fleet worker c_naive, session 5 of that worker's log (launched 2026-07-29 15:35:00 -0400), restart 16 of that session, rooted in randomized balanced XOR trees over the 32 raw inputs (root naive#1958, i.e. constructors.build("naive", 1958), no seeded circuit), which rebuilds to exactly the logged 146 gates at depth 3. Chain: root -> 88 gates at depth 6 at walk iteration 33873 (worker run-time t = 69192.7 s, 2026-07-30 10:48:12 -0400) -> this 88 at depth 5 at walk iteration 37155 (t = 69198.8 s, 2026-07-30 10:48:19 -0400), 6.1 s later by the walk's Pareto depth tie-break. All wall-clock times here are local, UTC-04:00, not UTC; t is measured from that session's start, so it is 19.22 h at the find. Quote the session as well as the restart - the log holds five worker sessions and 58 restarts in total, and there is an earlier restart 16 in a different session. Why nothing imported can be in that chain, strongest fact first: the ROOT reads nothing. The root spec was constructor:naive, and the constructor branch of the archived worker's root generator calls only constructors.build(name, seed) - it has no file-reading path at all, and every branch of that generator that can open a circuit off disk is a different branch, unreachable under this spec. The producing engine reads nothing either: both the 88 at depth 6 and this circuit came out of walk chunks, and engine_walk has no candidate pool and no disk read path. The cross-pollination route is closed five ways: the knob (pop_glob) has exactly one writer repo-wide (worker.py:133); hunt_worker.py never sets it; the merge helper's single call site is guarded on that knob being set; the supervisor never launches worker.py at all, so no worker in this fleet had cross-pollination available; and the untouched log contains zero of the lines the engine emits when a merge brings material in. Family repulsion was off (repel=False on the session's start line), each restart carries its own local context (observable: restart 16 opens at cur=93 best=93, worse than restart 15's 92, so nothing carried over), there are no reseed files and no context adoption, and the worker never imports the archive module. Four corroborations a skeptic can recheck: (a) all five code files are byte-identical to the already-audited archive of mixcolumns_88gates_depth6 and predate this run by two days; (b) that published log archive is a byte-exact prefix of the live log and already contains this session's repel=False start line; (c) the mask set is line 35285 of the worker's own harvest file c_naive.pop.jsonl and appears in zero of the fleet's other fifteen harvest files (sixteen in total); (d) the RNG seed is arithmetically forced by the clock - seed 1958 at this restart implies 242 prior chunks, predicting t = 65340 s against 65349 s logged, 0.014 % off. It is not an isolated point: 135 distinct own-lineage 88-gate depth-5 mask sets were harvested in the same pocket, all oracle-verified, every one of them first appearing at or after that line (the record is one of the 135). circuits.claim: Realizes AES MixColumns in 88 two-input XOR gates at depth 5. This is NOT a new gate-count record: 88 is the existing best-known count, published by Jean (ePrint 2026/1481, posted 2026-07-23), and Jean has priority. What changed on 2026-07-30 is whose lineage reaches the (88, 5) point: it is now reached by a circuit found from scratch, rooted in a randomized XOR tree over the 32 raw inputs, rather than only by mixcolumns_88gates_depth5, whose seed chain runs through Jean's published work. That removes THIS PROJECT'S dependence on that circuit at the depth-5 point; it does not beat it. The consequence is that the two frontiers this repository used to state collapse into one: 97 @ 3, 92 @ 4, 88 @ 5, entirely on this project's own lineage and with no imported material. Comparisons: it dominates Jean's 88 at depth 7 (equal count, two levels shallower - with the standing caveat that depth 7 is this project's own measurement of its own transcription, because that note states no depth), improves on the published depth-5 point (94, Osvik and Canright, ePrint 2024/1076, Appendix F) by six gates, and dominates this project's own 88s at depths 6, 7 and 8 and its 89 at depth 5. Its depth 5 is forced, not merely observed: the ASAP least-fixpoint schedule over its own mask set - the shallowest schedule any circuit on that mask set admits - still puts 11 of its 32 output bits (rows 1, 7, 12, 13, 17, 18, 21, 25, 27, 28, 31) at depth 5, so it cannot be rescheduled to depth 4. It is a construction distinct from every other circuit here: the most internal masks it shares with any of them is 45, against the superseded mixcolumns_98gates_depth3 (Jaccard 0.319), while the largest Jaccard it reaches is 0.323, against mixcolumns_88gates_depth6 (43 masks) - which is also the largest against any other 88; the two maxima fall on different circuits because the 98 is a bigger mask set, and both are far below the 0.7 same-family threshold, and it shares 42 of 88 masks with Jean's circuit, 32 of which are the forced output targets, leaving 10 of 56 free masks in common. What no imported material does NOT claim: not method independence (the engines and knobs were tuned over a campaign that did read published circuits), not disjointness from Jean's circuit, not landscape independence, not optimality, and not bit-reproducibility of the descent - the root is exactly reproducible, the trajectory is not. Its remove-2 shell (1,540 windows) and remove-3 shell (27,720 windows) are exhaustively empty, so any 87-gate circuit differs from it by at least 4 masks. 87 was not found, and no optimality claim is made.
